title: The Hallel
lead: The Hallel ("praise") is Psalms 113–118, sung as one set at Passover and the other great festivals, in the temple and in synagogues to this day. The rabbis called it the "Egyptian Hallel" after 114:1, and called Psalm 136 the "Great Hallel". The hymn Jesus and his disciples sang after the Last Supper was probably its second half.

sections.b: Six psalms of praise stand together in the first part of Book Five: Psalm 113 praises the God who lifts the poor, 114 sings of the exodus, 115 mocks idols and blesses Israel, 116 gives thanks for rescue from death, 117 calls the nations, and 118 is a festival procession to the temple gates. The Mishnah has the Levites sing them while the Passover lambs were slaughtered and the family sing them at the Passover meal, part before the meal and part after it (Mishnah Pesachim 5:7; 10:6–7). The Talmud lists eighteen days a year for the full Hallel, among them the eight days of Booths and of Hanukkah (Bavli Arakhin 10a). Christians know the set from Mark 14:26 and from "Hosanna" and "Blessed is the one who comes" (Psalm 118:25–26; Mark 11:9).
